author: original (NevaIB)
title: Combined, conditional and independent events

points.text: Venn, tree and sample-space diagrams and tables of outcomes
Conditional probability from diagrams and tables

bigPicture: Combined events need a diagram: Venn diagrams for overlaps, trees for sequences, tables for two-way data. The diagram makes the rules almost automatic.

keyIdeas.answer: Venn diagram: overlapping events in one trial. Tree diagram: events in sequence (multiply along branches, add complete paths). Sample-space diagram or table: two dice, two-way data.
P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together: P(A ∩ B) = 0, so P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
P(A | B): restrict to the outcomes in B, then find the fraction of them also in A. On a tree, second-stage branches are already conditional.
A and B are independent if one happening does not change the probability of the other: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).

keyTerms.def: the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other

workedExamples.title: Venn
workedExamples.prompt: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, P(A ∩ B) = 0.15. Find P(A only) and P(neither).

misconceptions.right: If P(A), P(B) > 0, mutually exclusive events are dependent: one happening makes the other impossible.
Multiply along branches; add between paths.

practice.prompt: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7. Find P(A ∩ B) and determine whether A and B are independent.
60% of students take the bus. 10% of bus users are late, and 25% of other students are late. (a) Find P(late). (b) Given that a student is late, find the probability they took the bus.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
